label: D2: chose a2 but landed in S1 (rare transition a2->S1)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), when the state input is S1 and the action input is a2, i.e. the rare transition a2->S1. Everything at D2 is observed, so no future variables are used. Dev: P 0.91, R 0.95, F1 0.93, mass recall 0.99. It does not fire on D1 or GO, on the common a1->S1 transition (0.6% of mass), or on any S2 arrival. Magnitude, read from the example windows: it is near max (0.94-1.0) when the agent is firmly in an a2 / S2-good regime, and in the top windows the 1.00 activations come when the previous trial was rewarded. Weak activations (lowest quartile, ~0.05-0.3) come when the a2 choice is recent or S1 is good (just after a switch), so the magnitude seems to track how strongly the agent expected S2. Most misses are low-magnitude cases.

issues: None of my checks refuted the label. I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.909, R 0.945, F1 0.926, mass recall 0.992.
The phase claims hold. GO has essentially no mass (mass recall 1e-6), D1 has none (0), D2 arrivals at S2 have almost none (3e-7), and the common transition a1->S1 holds 0.6% of the mass.
The feature is specific to a2->S1, not to rare transitions in general. The predicate (phase==D2)&(common==0) has precision 0.50 because it also covers a1->S2, where the feature does not fire.

The false positives (about 9% of predicted steps) are not systematic. Precision stays between 0.83 and 0.94 across prev_reward, the previous trial's transition and action, stay, good state and trial position. The lowest values (0.83) are after a switch from a1, which matches the explanation's note about weak activation after a switch.
The misses are weak activations (0.01-0.15) on common a1->S1 arrivals and hold only 0.8% of the mass.

The magnitude claim checks out. When good==2 (S2 good), activation quartile coverage is 0.66/0.80/0.85 for the upper three quartiles, versus 0.27/0.12/0.06 when good==1. So the strong activations do come in the S2-good regime.
